title: Promptset Stability Gate & Actionability Contract for Optimize
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a stability gating mechanism and an actionability contract for Optimize evals that prevents regressions from reaching production while prioritizing measurable, customer-relevant impact. This ticket codifies required prompt set composition, statistical thresholds, A/B stopping rules, and rollback triggers for model rollouts and quantization/optimization changes.

Scope:
- Required promptset strata, seeding rules, and minimum per-stratum sample sizes.
- Multi-metric signal definitions (quality, hallucination, intent match, latency) and how they combine into a composite stability score.
- Statistical tests, sample sizing, and confidence bounds for canaries/A-B.
- Concrete rollback triggers and an escalation ladder (automated and manual).
- Integration points with Console alerts, Optimize dashboards, and rollout automation.

Out of scope:
- Core runtime kernel changes (ENG to own separate tickets).
- Full UI redesign of Console; we will use existing alerting panels and add new widgets in a follow-up ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Promptset composition: For every Optimize evaluation, the promptset must include: 4 strata (core functional, edge-cases, adversarial, long-tail customer samples) with at least 200 seeds in aggregate and >=30 seeds per stratum for initial canaries; documented seed selection method.

2) Stability Gate metric: A composite stability score is computed per canary consisting of: weighted quality F1 (0.5), hallucination rate (0.2), intent-match recall (0.2), median latency (0.1). Score range normalized to 0-100 and documented in the spec.

3) Regression thresholds: Rollout blocked if composite stability score degrades by >=3.0 points with p<0.05 using two-sided bootstrap test on stratified samples, OR if any single-signal degradation exceeds pre-defined absolute deltas (quality -2.5 pts, hallucination +1.5% absolute, intent-match -3.0 pts, median latency +25%).

4) A/B test rules: Minimum sample size per variant = 1,000 requests or 7 days of traffic for public canaries; use sequential testing with alpha=0.05 and pre-specified maximum test length of 21 days; stop early if cross-metric rejection conditions met (see metrics_and_signals).

5) Long-tail sentinel: For customers with >1% of traffic, run per-customer sentinel checks on a 24h window; if any customer-level composite score degrades by >=5 points, automatically pause traffic for that customer and create high-priority alert in PagerDuty.

6) Rollback automation: Rollouts must include an automated rollback policy that triggers when canary composite score fails stability gate or when any absolute single-signal threshold is breached; rollback must revert traffic within 5 minutes of trigger when running on Dedicated/Hosted clusters with autoscaling enabled.

7) Observability hooks: Evaluate events, signal deltas, and the statistical test outputs are logged to Console for every canary run; dashboards expose per-stratum breakdown and a downloadable CSV of raw prompt-level results.
8) Documentation: A concise PRD and runbook are published with examples, decision flow, and links to sample Jupyter notebooks for rerunning tests locally.
implementation_plan: 1) Finalize promptset seeding algorithm and central repository schema (PM + Eng spike).
2) ENG implements composite score calculator and exposes REST endpoint returning per-stratum summaries.
3) Instrument Console: add canary pipeline view, per-stratum charts, and automated alert rules for the defined thresholds.
4) Create rollout automation: implement policy YAML that accepts stability-gate thresholds and ties into existing rollout engine for canary -> gradual -> full.
5) Run 3 shadow/canary experiments across different model families (base, quantized, optimized runtime) and capture metrics to tune weights and thresholds.
6) Post-launch: collect 30 days of telemetry and re-evaluate threshold calibration; iterate policy if false positives exceed 5% of canaries.
rollout_plan: Canary profile A (internal): 0% -> 1% traffic for 24h -> evaluate; stop if gate fails.
Canary profile B (public small): 0% -> 5% traffic over 3 days with sequential testing; evaluate daily and stop if any per-stratum p<0.05 degradation appears.
Full rollout: only after 3 consecutive successful canaries and 7 days of stable metrics; automated rollback policy attached to deployment manifest.
Emergency stop: any PD alert tagged 'optimize-stability' pauses traffic immediately; SRE and PM receive automatic escalation.
metrics_and_signals: Primary signals: composite stability score, quality-F1, hallucination-rate, intent-match-recall, median and 95th percentile latency.
Secondary signals: token-rate cost delta, CPU/GPU utilization, error rates (5xx), memory paging events.

Statistical tests: stratified bootstrap for composite score confidence intervals; sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for early A/B stopping on binary safety signals; Benjamini-Hochberg correction when testing >1 metric per canary.

Sample sizing guidance: for target detectable effect of 1.5 points on composite score with power=0.8 and alpha=0.05, recommend >=1,000 stratified requests per variant; smaller canaries allowed for exploratory but must be labeled 'informational'.
Alert thresholds: automatic 'warning' at 1.5 point composite delta, 'critical' at 3.0 points or any single-signal absolute threshold breach as specified in acceptance criteria.
notes_and_decisions: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting — aligned on need for a single composite gate + per-signal absolute thresholds. Action: PM to draft weights; Eng to prototype score exporter. (Asha, Luca, Mei)

2025-02-19: Engineering spike complete — prototype uses stratified sampling and exposes per-prompt results. Concern raised about weight sensitivity; decision to run calibration sweep across 3 customer workloads. (Luca)
2025-02-25: Design provided feedback that Console needs an interaction to 'pause per-customer' in addition to global pause. Added to rollout actions. (Ravi)
2025-03-03: SRE recommends increasing latency weight for ultra-low-latency customers; agreed to make weights configurable per-project by an override in rollout YAML. (Nadia)
Open question: How to surface prompt-level counterexamples to non-technical PMs — follow-up: add a 'redaction-safe' example view in Console.
